messages:
alex: Heads-up — hitting GPU quota ceilings during the canary burst. We need an emergency quota increase to avoid dropping traffic. filing this thread for approvals and routing.

alex: Summary: project=prod-serving-2024, billing=ops-billing-01. Regions impacted: us-central1 + europe-west1. Workload: canary rollout for new batching+kv-cache optimizer (short 24–72h burst).

alex: Requested increases: 
- us-central1: +12 L4 (total target 40), +8 A100 (total target 24)
- europe-west1: +4 A100 (total target 12)
- global: external IP quota increase to 60 (we create ephemeral EIPs for burst pools)

alex: Cost note: estimated incremental cost ~ $5k/day at peak (GPU hours), finance okayed spike window if pre-approved. tagging @maria for billing + @sam for capacity sign-off. :eyes:

maria: Thanks. Can you paste the GCP quota form fields you plan to submit? need exact numbers for finance ticket. Also confirm billing account id.

alex: Draft copy of form answers: 
- Project ID: prod-serving-2024
- Billing account: 01A1B2-ops-billing-01
- Quota type: GPUs (NVIDIA A100), GPUs (NVIDIA L4), Static External IPs
- Region: us-central1, europe-west1 (for region-specific quotas)
- Current quota: A100(us-central1)=16, A100(europe-west1)=8, L4(us-central1)=28, External IPs=45
- Requested new totals: A100(us-central1)=24, A100(europe-west1)=12, L4(us-central1)=40, External IPs=60
- Justification: Canary rollout of optimized runtime requires transient increased parallel model endpoints to validate latency and correctness under production load. Ramp expected 24–72hrs. Workload is customer-facing; rollback if errors.

alex: gcloud / diagnostic bits we ran (copied to avoid re-running):
```
gcloud compute regions describe us-central1 --project=prod-serving-2024
gcloud compute project-info describe --project=prod-serving-2024
# output shows current quotas above
```

sam: +1 from infra on capacity. please include the oncall runbook link and the exact start/end window in the quota request (GCP likes a time-bound justification). Also include contact: infra-oncall@redwood.com.

alex: Will add window: start=2026-03-22T18:00Z end=2026-03-25T06:00Z. Oncall runbook: https://playbooks.internal/redwood/oncall/gpu-burst

julie: Small ops notes:
- If they ask about IP addresses, mention we use ephemeral EIPs for per-pool NAT and will release after burst.
- VPC peering and router SNAT rules are ready in eu-west1 but need network-team approval for additional NAT entries; looping @sam.

maria: Finance: please cc finance-ops@redwood.com when you submit so we can track cost center tagging. I approve the spend for the timeboxed window.

alex: Filing the GCP quota request now, will paste the request link. If GCP asks for proof-of-need, I can attach perf charts and the canary results.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started (canary-id: canary-2026-03-22-18). Monitoring latency and GPU utilization.

alex: GCP request submitted: https://console.cloud.google.com/iam-admin/quotas?project=prod-serving-2024&requestId=RQ-1866004321 (internal link)

sam: I'll approve on our side once support-case shows. Also confirm whether we want to convert any of these to reserved Dedicated capacity if this pattern repeats — we should discuss with product next week.

alex: Noted. I'll follow up w/ product. For now we need the temporary quota. tagging network for NAT approval.

julie: Quick checklist for post-approval: 
- Add ephemeral EIP release automation (lambda)
- Validate IAM for service account that will create instances (svc-gpu-burst)
- Update routing policy to allow cross-region fallback

alex: Thanks all. I'll update thread when GCP responds. :thumbsup:
